 Judgment

1. The judgment shall dispose of appeals bearing MA Nos. 137/2018 & 131/2018 and also MA No.
3/2021, infact cross objections filed in MA No. 137/2018 treated as appeal by the court, as they arise out of the same award and the common judgment passed by the court of learned Principal District Judge, Jammu vide dated 29.05.2018.

2. The lands of the respondents-claimants as mentioned in the appeals situate at Village Channi Rama, Tehsil and District, Jammu were acquired by the appellants after the indent was placed by the Defence Estate Officer for defence purposes.
The proceedings were initiated under the Land Acquisition Act by the Collector.
The Collector assessed the compensation of the land @ 6 lacs per kanal.
The claimants were also held entitled to Jabrana as mentioned in the award passed by the a/w connected matters Collector vide dated 10.05.2007.
The claimants being not satisfied with the amount of compensation awarded by the Collector filed applications for reference in terms of Section 18 of the J&K land Acquisition Act.
The reference was decided by the court of learned Principal District Judge, Jammu vide dated 29.05.2018 which is impugned in the present appeal.
The learned District Court clubbed two references and decided the same by common judgment.
The Reference Court enhanced compensation in favour of the claimants from Rs. 6 lacs per kanal to Rs.20 lacs per kanal.

The claimants were also held entitled to Jabrana @ 15% and interest @ 6% on Union Of India vs Hari Om And Others on 5 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178388400/
1

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the increased compensation from the date of acquisition till payment is made by the respondents.

3. The grounds agitated in the appeal for setting aside the judgment are that the District Judge has not enhanced the compensation in favour of the respondents-claimants as per the rate of compensation that was required to be allowed when viewed in the light of the date of acquisition of land.

That the reliance upon the report of Tehsildar, Narayan Singh is misconceived as no legal value can be attached to the same as the same pertains to the period after 39 months of issuance of notice in terms of Sections 6 & 7 of the Land Acquisition Act.

It is further stated that the price of small developed piece of land cannot determine the price of large chunk of land as it will not be possible to find out a willing purchaser for big chunk of land.
The appellants have also challenged the interest awarded by the court in favour of the claimants.
a/w connected matters 4.
The respondents-claimants have appeared through counsel and contested the present appeal.
5. The scanned record of the District Court is before the court.
6. Mr. Sandeep Gupta, CGSC appearing for appellant has argued as per the averments contained in the appeal.

Elaborating the stand taken in the appeal, the counsel has argued that the reliance placed by the learned District Judge upon the statement of Tehsildar or the circle rates which came into existence after the land was acquired is not as per law.
The court has also made a mistake in holding that 99 feet of land is in front and, therefore, the market value has been assessed according to the same.
The interest is also not as per the law as there was no reason to award the interest from the date mentioned in the judgment.
Infact it is pleaded that there was no evidence produced on behalf of the claimants which could prompt the court to fix the compensation @ 20 lacs per kanal in favour of the claimants.

7. Mr. S.M.Choudhary, learned counsel appearing for the claimants- respondents has argued that the learned District Judge has infact granted less compensation than the one which was due to the claimants.
Otherwise, the reliance by the District Judge upon the report of the Tehsildar or the circle rates cannot be faulted with.
8. The claimants, namely, Hari Om, Reena Dogra, Kanta Devi, Lalit Magotra, Nathu Ram and Narayan Singh have recorded their statements in reference.
Choudhary Aslam Din and Vinod Kumar Lakhan Pal have a/w connected matters recorded their statements for the respondent-appellant herein before the reference court.

9. As far as the statements of Hari Om, Kanta Devi, Lalit Magotra are concerned, they have referred to the report of Settlement Naib Tehsildar Bahu, Jammu and Tehsildar, Jammu to canvas before the court that the market rate of land of the claimants was Rs.25 lacs per kanal.
They have mentioned of the escalation of the rates from the year 2006.

They have also mentioned of the circular issued by the Deputy Commissioner, Jammu where the circle rate of commercial nature in Channi Rama area Union Of India vs Hari Om And Others on 5 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178388400/
2 was fixed at Rs.40 lacs per kanal and seek that much of compensation of the land acquired by the Collector.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. PW-Prof. Lalit Magotra in his statement also states that the rate of land increased from Rs.25 lacs to Rs.40 lacs per kanal within the short span.
11. PW-Reena Dogra has filed the affidavit as piece of evidence and the same is in consonance with what has been stated by other witnesses of which mention is made above.

12. PW-Nathu Ram has brought the record regarding stamp duty rate issued by the Deputy Commissioner (Collector), Jammu for the year 2007-2008 and as per the same the commercial rate of Village Channi Rama was Rs.40 lacs, commercial B rate was Rs.30 lacs and agriculture rate was Rs.25 lacs per kanal.
As per the witness, there was no circular of stamp duty rate in the year 2005-2006.
a/w connected matters 13.

PW-Narayan Singh has also appeared as witness for the claimants and was posted as Tehsildar,
Jammu in the year 2006.

He has given the report dated 03.10.2006 marked as 'EXP-NS1' and as per the witness he had recommended the market rate of the land in question at Rs.25 lacs per kanal on the basis of report of Patwari and Naib Tehsildar as the land acquired was on the front side of the National Highway.
As per the witness, the commercial rate in the year 2006-2007 was more than Rs.25 lacs.
He has also stated that the rate of land on the front side of National Highway is commercial rate and the land at some distance or on the back side is having different rates.
14. RW-Choudhary Aslam Din has deposed that he was posted as Naib Tehsildar, Bahu in September, 2006.
The report dated 25.09.2006 was prepared by him and identified the signature on the same.
He had recommended the market rate of land as Rs.25 lacs per kanal.
The six years average rate was prepared by Patwari on the instructions of Tehsildar concerned.
The market rate was assessed on enquiry.
The khasra numbers mentioned in the report are on the front side of the National Highway.
15. RW-Vinod Kumar Lakhan Pal has no knowledge of the acquisition proceedings and has only deposed that the defence department had deposited compensation.
He is not in know of the land acquired in the proceedings.

16. The perusal of the judgment impugned in the appeal reveals that the court has mainly relied upon the statement of PW-Narayan Singh and a/w connected matters RW-Aslam Din and report prepared by them dated 03.10.2006 which reflected the market value of the land in question to the tune of Rs.25 lacs per kanal.
The land in question is mostly on the front side of the National Highway is not much in dispute.

The court has also taken note of the circle rate at Channi Rama area for the year 2007-2008 which was fixed as Rs. 40 lacs per kanal for commercial purposes,
determined by the government.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Admittedly, no Sale Deed was produced by the applicants before the reference court in support of their contention that their land acquired on behalf of the appellant had market value of Rs.40 lacs per kanal in the year 2006.

It may also be noted herein that the applicants had filed affidavits by way of evidence before the reference court and had relied upon the report of the Tehsildar and also circle rate fixed by the Deputy Commissioner as Rs.40 lacs per kanal for the year 2007-2008.

It was also submitted through affidavits that there is escalation of 30% from 25.09.2006 to 10.05.2007 in the rate of Rs.25 lacs per kanal, determined by the Tehsildar, which otherwise come to Rs.32.05 lacs per kanal.

18. It may be mentioned herein that the Collector had fixed the compensation of the lands in question at the rate of Rs.6 lacs per kanal as per the rate approved by the Committee of Collectors on 21.09.2005 in respect of land measuring 40 kanals situate in Village Channi Rama though the Collector had acknowledged of his own that the reasonable rate of the land being a prime one, it should be Rs.9 lacs per kanal.
The Collector had also referred to the report of the Tehsildar on which the a/w connected matters applicants also relied upon before the Reference Court though not finally agreeing with the same.

19. As far as the argument raised by the learned counsel appearing for the appellant that the circle rate fixed by the Deputy Commissioner for the year 2007-2008 is concerned the same cannot be suo moto taken as market rate of the land in question as the same is in order to have minimum stamp duty from the parties to the transactions cannot be brushed aside.
Moreso when the same is for the period which was not the one when the notice under Section 4 or 6 of the Land Acquisition Act was issued for the purposes of acquisition of land.
The court is not made aware of any report which may have become the basis for fixation of circle rate by the Deputy Commissioner.

The report of the Tehsildar marked as annexure 'EXPT-NS-1' with the record file and the statement recorded of the Tehsildar-Narayan Singh issuing this document assesses the market value as Rs.25 lacs per kanal of the land acquired.

The report of the Tehsildar is based upon the report prepared by the Patwari Halqa of Channi Rama and endorsed by the then Naib Tehsildar Bahu, Jammu, namely, Chowdhary Aslam Din, who also appeared as a witness though for the State and he has also stated that the Patwari had entered the average rate of the land in the report and that he had also asked the people about the market rate during the enquiry.
It means that the market rate was confirmed as Rs.25 lacs per kanal of the lands in question by the Tehsildar on the report prepared by Patwari and Naib Tehsildar of the concerned area.
a/w connected matters 20.

The reference court was in the absence of any Sale Deed or any other document evidencing the market value of the land acquired was left with no other option but to mainly rely upon the report of Tehsildar which was prepared around the time when the notification for acquisition of land was issued by the Collector.
It can be well presumed that the report by the revenue officials was prepared after due enquiry and taking all the attending circumstances and cannot be ignored.

21. The court is of the view that the market rate assessed by the Tehsildar to the tune of Rs.25 lacs per kanal can be the basic criteria for determining compensation of the lands with some margin as it Union Of India vs Hari Om And Others on 5 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178388400/
4

entities.text: Union Of India vs Hari Om And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: cannot also be said at the same time that the report by the revenue officials will reflect the precise assessment of the lands.

The reference court has assessed the compensation @ Rs.20 lacs per kanal and the court finds no fault in the same after curtailing the market rate determined by the revenue officials to that extent from the one determined as Rs.25 lacs per kanal.
The exact market value of the land cannot be assessed and some presumption has to be drawn while assessing the same.

This is what has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 2015(15) SCC 220.
22.

Incidentally, in the case in hand the applicants did not bother to place on record any sale deed as stated above or any other documentary evidence which could provide better picture regarding the market rate of the land of the applicants during the reference proceedings.
The court finds no reason to either enhance the compensation as sought for by the claimants in the present proceedings.
a/w connected matters 23.

The court, thus, finds no error in the judgment of reference court qua the compensation assessed of the land acquired of the respondents herein @ Rs.20 lacs per kanal along with Jabrana at rate of 15% and the interest of 6% on the increased amount from the date of acquisition till the payment is made by the appellants herein.
The judgment passed by the reference court is upheld.
24. The appeals filed by the appellants-Union of India are, accordingly, dismissed.
The cross appeal filed by the respondents-claimants and treated as appeal by this court also stands dismissed.
25. The copy of the judgment shall be placed on all the files.
